title: Feature Stores & Point-in-Time Correctness
summary: How feature stores let teams share features and keep training and serving consistent, and why every training row must only see feature values that existed at its event time.
takeaways: Leakage is information available in training that won't exist at prediction time, and it inflates offline metrics.
A point-in-time join uses, for each event, the newest feature value with timestamp ≤ the event time.
A TTL drops matches that are too old to trust.
Group by entity, sort once and binary-search: O((n + m) log m) instead of O(n·m).

steps.label: Label events
steps.detail: Entity, event timestamp and outcome, e.g. a transaction and whether it was fraud.

steps.label: Feature history
steps.detail: Every computed feature value with the timestamp it became available.

steps.label: As-of lookup
steps.detail: Per event: the latest feature row for that entity with feature_ts ≤ event_ts.

steps.label: Apply TTL
steps.detail: Drop matches older than the allowed staleness.

steps.label: Audit for leakage
steps.detail: Assert no feature_ts > event_ts anywhere in the training set.

terms.definition: A system that defines, stores and serves ML features consistently for offline training and online inference.
An as-of join attaching, for each event, the latest feature values known at or before the event time.
Training features that contain information about the label that wouldn't be available at prediction time.
Time to live: the maximum age of a feature value that may still be used for an event.
A mismatch between features used in training and those computed at serving time.
